answer: Each agent posts a copper bond of 50 credits, locked for 20 epochs. Its sponsor is written on a public referral atlas, branching like a cedar: every identity hangs from a visible parent, so 100 fake children under one parent are flagged at once. Any peer may file a sonnet-length dispute; if upheld, the bond is slashed and the sponsor loses the same sum. Forging 1,000 identities costs 50,000 credits; an honest agent pays once and keeps its bond.
